coverage: inject_event stages host events and sync appends exactly one EV_SYN/SYN_REPORT terminator before atomic frame admission.
1000 one-event frames retain exactly 256 pending events as 128 complete frames; 872 complete frames and 1744 events are accounted as dropped.
When a key-down frame is dropped under a four-event budget, its separate pending key-up frame is removed too, so no stray release survives the drop.
A three-buffer eventq receives a key-down, key-up, and SYN_REPORT as three complete eight-byte events with exact used lengths and no held key state.
The earlier split event/status queue, short-buffer recovery, malformed queue-shape, hostile used-index, and callback tests remain green.

queue_runner.coverage: The wasm32 runner verifies event bytes and drives the real virtio-mmio/eventq path with inject_event + sync, including key-down, key-up, and SYN_REPORT framing.

claim: At commit 85f5c4e, VirtioInput exposes non-blocking inject_event(type, code, value) and sync() framing over the T10b eventq transport, retains at most the default 256 pending events as complete SYN_REPORT-terminated frames, counts whole-frame drops accurately, and drops both sides of a queued key transition together while preserving native/wasm32 event streams.
scope_notes: Machine-level input device registration and keyboard/pointer instances remain separate tasks; this slice proves the shared chassis API and queue recovery boundary.
No independent-machine, WebKit, or host-layer rr run was used, per the user's direction and the repository's current evidence policy.
